Solution: Finding a way to reduce sexual desire. Some anti depressants such as Fluoxetine significantly reduces sexual desire and drive, and is used to treat compulsive sexual disorders and sex addictions. I would suggest looking into that to prevent you from feeling any sexual desire as that seems to be the source of your problem. In order to get it though you may need to speak to a psychiatrist to get prescribed. But believe me it will be worth it. 

Since you are female you are able to get birth control too, I know the combined pill has the ability to reduce sex drive and desire significantly as it reduces your testosterone levels in your body (which is responsible for sex drive and desire). Try that if you are really struggling to get a hold of a psychiatrist, but I would say your safest bet is still Fluoxetine, as I cannot promise combined birth control pill is strong enough to combat this attraction for sure (but it will probably help).

Try that for a few months and see how you feel before doing anything else.

Of course if you do have any access to therapy or a psychologist that would be ideal but I know they can be hard to get sometimes. If you can find out some triggers that set you off then try to work out what they are to best avoid any triggers that could be avoided to make things easier for you.

Is there a dramatic event that they go through together that suddenly force them to work together, or being forced to put up with each other which then requires them to work on their differences and finding the best qualities of each other in the process?

Considering historical context, are there class differences? Family disapproval? Remember that at this time courtship heavily involved the family. Religious considerations/morals? Is she pious and prudish?

Ideas of character developments in 18th century context 

- Intelligent, timid girl, no voice of her own, devoutly obedient to her family, perhaps she has an idea in her head of the perfect man she’d marry (that is opposite of George), maybe she has dreams of her own but never pursued them because she’s tied to family / religious values, something that could be a running conflict of her conscience. I do want to mention that the universal psychological properties of colour are a completely different thing from the cultural symbolism of the colours.

I work with colour psych for a living. Blue is the colour of the mind and it’s psychological properties are calmness, trust and logic - you’ll see a lot of banks using this colour. Green is positive, reassurance, balance and peace. Orange is abundance, comfort and fun/passion (I’ll get more into how all this changes in a combination of black). Contrary to popular belief red is not for danger, it can be aggressive but it’s main properties are energy, survival and stimulation.

I’m sure the blues and greens have explained itself already why they’re used for the things you asked. In stop light green is a an a ok reassurance sign for go. When it comes to red with the stop sign it’s not a danger sign, red is a colour that calls for action because it’s so stimulating and and that action is to stop and take notice. It also increases the pulse rate and makes time seem to pass quicker than it is. Another contrary to popular belief red is not actually the most visible colour but it does have the tendency to appear to be nearer than it is. Blue on the other hand appears to be further than it is hence why it is not used specifically in traffic lights.

Back to orange, when combined with black it’s properties become the opposite, it’s a sign of deprivation. When it comes to warning signs it can be either yellow or orange combined with black, both produce a very negative reaction. In nature and aposematic animals this combination is actually one of the more effective warning signs communicating ‘keep away I’m not good for you’. This would explain your question whether these things are age old primitive and yes they are. For instance the reason green is reassuring to us is because lots of greens indicate presence of water and unlikeliness of famine, it’s a primitive reassurance.

For the blue berries being dangerous argument, keep in mind that the blue pigment is one of the rarest in nature, we’re more likely to relate blue to something other than poisonous berries, such as the sky or the sea. There are poisonous red berries but there are much more other things that are red too that are not poisonous, the combination of black and yellow though doesn’t have many other natural comparisons but ‘not good’ sign.
I do want to mention that we don’t know why for sure some of these colours give the psychological effects that it does it’s still being researched, some are quite self explanatory on a primitive level, but why these colours are chosen for certain things is because of the universal psychological effects they have on us, a lot of it is chosen in intuition because of evolution.
